problem: The Aiden meeting room could appear motionless when the runtime was slow, blocked, or raised an exception because the browser waited silently on a synchronous request.

root_cause.server: The local HTTP server used a single-threaded synchronous request path and did not wrap Aiden runtime calls with timeout or exception notices.
root_cause.browser: The composer did not optimistically display the owner message, show runtime progress, disable duplicate sends, or enforce a browser timeout.

implemented: Added ThreadingHTTPServer so a slow runtime request does not freeze the local server.
Added a server-side runtime watchdog using AIDEN_MESSENGER_RUNTIME_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
Added governed runtime notice payloads for timeout and error paths.
Added browser-side pending owner messages, busy status, disabled send state, AbortController timeout, and visible system notices.
Added CSS states for pending, busy, warning, and error visibility.
CIEU_behavior: Runtime watchdog notices include CIEU/CZL five-tuple fields and tell the owner the correct path instead of silently failing.
limitations: A timeout notice does not cancel an already-running Python worker thread; it prevents silent UI stalls and keeps the server responsive.
This milestone fixes visibility and recoverability, not the deeper runtime latency of Aiden retrieval/brain/governance paths.
next_recommended_milestone: Optimize the Aiden meeting room reply path so lightweight memo/chat turns use fast retrieval and defer heavy strategy/runtime cycles unless explicitly requested.
